thread:
maya-marketing: hey team — prepping copy & slides for next week's launch. we need reproducible benchmark artifacts from runtime for the quantized long-context model runs. specifically:
- coldstart vs warmup profiles (p50/p95/p99) across seq lengths 512/2048/8192
- raw traces (kv/cache hits, batch sizes, per-token latency) + the exact warmup traffic used
- exact config + env (kernel, cudnn/cuda, quant flags, batcher settings) and seed list for RNGs
- a rerun with stable seeds and the same payloads used internally so marketing can package raw samples

Can runtime take this on? target: artifacts + a one-pager explaining methodology by Thu EOD. cc @simon-runtime @eli-eng

simon-runtime: thanks maya. quick clarifying q's: which model/quant variant and hardware? and do you need TSV of per-request traces or aggregated csvs? also, what does "raw traces" mean for marketing — full proto payloads or anonymized snippets?

maya-marketing: model = rw-7B-q4-v2 (quantized profile we used in last bench). hardware = any A100/RTX8000 equivalent is fine, but please note which. we prefer full per-request traces (anonymized payloads ok) so we can pull example prompts. aggregated csvs for charts would be great too.

eli-eng: we can run on a small dedicated pool. timeline: baseline run today (smoke), full rerun tomorrow morning. deliverables: 1) s3://redwood-marketing/bench/rw-7B-q4-v2/{date}/traces.tar.gz 2) csv percentiles per seq_len 3) runbook.md with exact commands and env. is that acceptable?

maya-marketing: perfect. please include the warmup ramp script and the exact seed values. marketing will need the command we used so the audit doc is concrete. also please record gen config (temperature/top_k) used for sample capture.

anya-pm: tiny ask — can we also capture coldstart memory stats (GPU mem alloc timeline) and the first 50 token latencies as separate artifact? helps the slide showing startup overhead.

simon-runtime: yes. plan:
1) Smoke run now to validate harness (5mins).
2) Full rerun tomorrow 0900-1100 UTC with fixed seeds and the marketing payload set. will capture: per-request trace proto (anonymized), per-token latency, kv-cache hit events, batch size timeline, GPU mem timeline.
3) Produce aggregated csvs: p50/p90/p95/p99 across seq 512/2048/8192 and coldstart vs warmed.

simon-runtime: commands we'll execute (example):
```bash
# warmup ramp (pseudo)
for s in 1 2 4 8 16; do
  ./bench_client --model rw-7B-q4-v2 --seq_len 2048 --batch $s --warmup_steps 20 --seed 12345 >> warmup.log
done

# actual run
./bench_client --model rw-7B-q4-v2 --seq_len {512,2048,8192} --batcher-config batcher.json --quant=q4 --seed-list seeds.txt --trace-out traces/ --metrics csvs/
```

eli-eng: we'll include a seeds.txt (50 seeds) and the exact payload bundle. seeds.txt will be uploaded alongside traces.

maya-marketing: can you add a short note in the runbook about how we handled non-determinism (tokenizer versions, any nondet ops)? we need to answer potential auditor Qs.

simon-runtime: yes — we'll capture git hashes for tokenizer, runtime, kernel. also note quantization path and whether we used JIT kernels.

runtime-ci-bot: job scheduled: bench-rw7b-q4-full-rerun (id: brq4-2026-03-24-0900). artifacts will be pushed to s3 on completion. ETA ~2.5h.

maya-marketing: awesome. last thing — can you name one sample prompt in the artifact root as "marketing-readme.txt" with the anonymized example we can include in the press kit? nothing sensitive, just the input and the model output we observed.

simon-runtime: yes — we'll add marketing-readme.txt with 3 anonymized samples and the exact gen config used for each.

eli-eng: tagging @ops to ensure S3 access and retention policy (we'll set 90 days then archive).

maya-marketing: thank you! this is exactly what we need. i'll follow up if legal wants additional redaction. :party_parrot:
